archetypes.name: cross-doc-resume-consistency
archetypes.rationale: The diff migrates mid-loop resumes from direct run-step3-review.sh calls to the design-step3-review.sh wrapper across SKILL.md, approval-gates.md, plan-review.md, and review-design-step3-loop.md; verifying no stale direct-call paths remain requires reading every changed reference doc and cross-checking them.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every file in the diff for residual references to `run-step3-review.sh --mode loop --starting-round` that should have been replaced with the new `design-step3-review.sh --starting-round` wrapper pattern. Also check that stall-recovery.md (referenced in test-implement-structure.sh checks for `step-8-ship.sh`, `run_in_background: true`, `timeout: 21600000`, and `<task-notification>`) was updated in this diff or already contains those strings; if it is absent from the diff, flag the gap. Verify that the `STEP3_RESUME_ROUND` binding is introduced before every mid-loop resume path in SKILL.md and that all four `STEP3_REVIEW_LOOP_STATUS` bail-out branches use `$STEP3_RESUME_ROUND` rather than inline fallback expressions. Check whether any prose in approval-gates.md still instructs callers to invoke `run-step3-review.sh` directly for Gate B resume idempotency. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: background-contract-completeness
archetypes.rationale: Switching long-running fences to run_in_background:true introduces a new contract: every backgrounded invocation must be followed by a task-notification wait before consuming result files; missing or misplaced waits can cause silent stale-read races that are hard to reproduce.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each script promoted to immediate-background mode in this diff (design-step3-review.sh initial launch, design-step3-review.sh resume fence, design-step5c.sh, design-step-final-summary.sh, run-step5-review.sh, step-7a.sh, step-8-ship.sh, and run-step-checks.sh fences), verify that SKILL.md contains an explicit `Wait for <task-notification>` instruction between the closing fence and the first result-file read or step-advancement prose. Pay particular attention to step-7a.sh: test-implement-structure.sh does not check for a task-notification wait near it — confirm whether a wait instruction is present in SKILL.md near that fence or intentionally absent. Evaluate whether the proximity window sizes used in `contains_near` (900 chars) and `require_near` (1400 chars) are large enough given the density of surrounding prose in the SKILL.md files; if any immediate-background fence is separated from its wait instruction by more prose than the window covers, flag it. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
